input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view with side-by-side and diff modes in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers a run comparison capability in the Dashboard: users select
two or more training or pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics
side by side, with a diff presentation that highlights which parameters and
metrics changed between two selected runs. This gives data scientists
in-platform visibility into what changed between candidate runs, replacing the
current exported-spreadsheet workflow that model promotion decisions depend on.

## Scope

- Add multi-run selection from the existing runs list (two or more runs).
- Render a comparison view showing the parameters and metrics of every
  selected run side by side.
- Provide a diff presentation of the comparison that highlights which
  parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs (values that
  differ between the two runs are visually distinguished from identical
  values).
- Read run parameters and metrics from the same per-run metadata already
  surfaced on run detail pages, covering both training runs and Data Science
  Pipelines runs.
- Comparison operates within the project the runs belong to; cross-project and
  cross-cluster comparison is out of scope per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a user has selected two or more runs in the runs list, when they open
  the comparison, then the parameters and metrics of all selected runs are
  displayed side by side.
- Given two runs are selected for comparison, when the diff presentation is
  shown, then the parameters and metrics that changed between the two runs are
  highlighted and distinguishable from unchanged values.
- Given runs of both kinds are selected (training runs and Data Science
  Pipelines runs), when the comparison is opened, then parameters and metrics
  for both kinds of runs are displayed (validates that the passive Data
  Science Pipelines component keeps working with no code change on its side).
- The comparison view is reachable from the runs list without leaving the
  project scope of the selected runs.
- The midstream build pipeline for the Dashboard repository is green with
  these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters
  and metrics side by side in the Dashboard — covered by the multi-run
  selection and side-by-side comparison view.
- **HLR-3 (P1)**: Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters
  and metrics changed between two selected runs — covered by the diff
  presentation of the same comparison surface. Bundled with HLR-1 rather than
  split: the diff view is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface
  over the same run parameters and metrics (same component, same team), and
  the strategy notes these requirements were consolidated from two customer
  councils with overlapping wording; splitting would build the same UI surface
  twice and is not independently deferrable.

# Link registered model versions to source runs and open comparison from the Model Registry

## Description

This epic delivers run lineage in the Model Registry: registered model versions
record a link back to the run that produced them, and a user browsing the
registry can open a run comparison starting from a registered model version.
This lets model promotion decisions start from the registry — the catalog of
record for candidate models — instead of requiring users to hunt for the
originating runs manually.

## Scope

- Record, on each registered model version, the link to the run that produced
  it (the mechanism — e.g. an existing metadata/extension point on model
  versions — is an implementation decision for the Model Registry team).
- Surface the source-run link in the Model Registry user experience.
- Provide an entry point from a registered model version (and/or its linked
  run) that opens the Dashboard run comparison for the linked run.
- Capture the run identity at registration time or via backfill for model
  versions registered while the lineage capability is being introduced, as the
  team's implementation design determines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version was registered from a run, when a user views that
  model version in the Model Registry, then the version shows the link back to
  the run that produced it.
- Given a model version with a linked run, when the user opens the comparison
  entry point, then the Dashboard run comparison opens for the linked run
  (verified against the Dashboard comparison capability; the entry point
  targets the comparison view via a link, so this epic proceeds in parallel
  with the Dashboard-side work and this criterion gates on the linked view
  resolving correctly).
- The midstream build pipeline for the Model Registry repository is green
  with these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)**: Registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry — covered by the
  lineage link and the comparison entry point.

# Document the run comparison workflow from the runs list and the Model Registry

## Description

This epic delivers user documentation for the run comparison workflow: how to
select runs and compare their parameters and metrics side by side, how to read
the diff highlighting between two runs, and how to open a comparison from a
registered model version in the Model Registry.

## Scope

- New documentation topic(s) covering the comparison workflow starting from
  the runs list: selecting two or more runs, reading the side-by-side
  parameters and metrics, and using the diff presentation between two runs.
- New documentation topic(s) covering the comparison workflow starting from
  the Model Registry: following a model version's link back to its source run
  and opening the comparison from there.
- Screenshots and procedure steps reflecting the implemented behavior of both
  entry points.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers the comparison workflow from the runs list, including
  multi-run selection, the side-by-side view, and the diff presentation
  between two runs.
- Documentation covers the comparison workflow from the Model Registry,
  including the model-version-to-run link and opening the comparison from the
  registry.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented
  comparison capability (both the Dashboard runs-list path and the
  registry-originated path) before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the
  runs list and the registry — covered by the documentation topics above.
